newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch see Dfl 230 million 1996 budget improvement.
newsitem.headline: Dutch see Dfl 230 million 1996 budget improvement.

text.p: The Dutch finance ministry will report a further 230 million guilder improvement in central government finances in its autumn progress report on the 1996 budget, government sources said on Monday.
Half of the windfall is due to increased revenues from natural gas production and half can be accounted for by decreased European Union contributions, the sources said.
They said the autumn report would likely be discussed in the Dutch cabinet next Friday and would be presented to parliament within the next two or three weeks.

Algemeen Dagblad newspaper said on Monday the running total improvement in the budgetary position for 1996 now stood at 850 million guilders, adding Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm wanted to use the windfall to further cut the government deficit.
Government sources confirmed the total figure, 620 million guilders of which had already been noted in the spring progress report, but gave no comment on the likely use of the windfall.
Official budget forecasts published in September showed a central government deficit of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1996 and 1997, versus 3.5 percent in 1995.
The broader measure of the public deficit under the European Monetary Union definition was forecast at 2.6 percent of GDP in 1996 and 2.2 percent in 1997, from 4.0 percent in 1995.
